asr.full_text: Hello everyone, welcome back, my name is Katherine Gu, I'm the head of product for Digital Assets at Solana Foundation. I'm really, truly excited to have Ari from TRM today with me to talk about SDP. Ari, welcome to the show, how you doing? I am so great and Katherine, as you know, I am a huge fan of yours and the work that's happening at Solana, so, yeah, no, thank you so much for having me on today. Yeah, tell us a little bit about yourself, your journey with TRM. Absolutely, can I tell process of doing a blog because I want to make sure that I'm having this opportunity to really like the content they should have. Because when I work on products, I try and make sure that they are available. I don't want to sell them but I want things to be that are out there. And I really hope that those products will sell out and that things that are out there will then be that are going to be available to people that are interested to like make a business that they can start making more money out of. Okay, so you know, right when you think about success. All your 130 episodes of TRM talks, I've done 100 plus podcasts, all the and every time I think of Solana and the ecosystem and the people building there, because I'm talking into this Mike, that was a gift from Solana. So so yes. So in terms of background, I'm Aerie Redford. I'm the Global Head of Policy at TRM Labs. We are a blockchain intelligence company, which means we work So, before we get into the talk, I want to take a moment to introduce myself. I'm the global head of policy at TRM Labs. We are a blockchain intelligence company, which means we work with law enforcement globally to track and trace illicit proceeds in cryptocurrency. We also work with regulators to make licensing determinate, help them make licensing determinations and ongoing supervision. And finally we work with the private sector. We work with teams from across the ecosystem. Think cryptocurrency exchanges, brokers, custodians, but also DFI protocols that are looking to screen wallets and do transaction monitoring to ensure that bad actors aren't engaging with their platforms. Yeah, I mean, I think it's really important what you just highlighted because, you know, as, you know, when we are designing Solana's development platform, the most important thing is it has to be enterprise ready, and it needs to have a lot of the compliance features baked in right from the start. So actually through the research, I realized TRM is actually the first compliance provider on Solana dated all the way back in 2021. So, I guess in your view, as you're looking at the Solana ecosystem as a whole, how do you think that compliance has improved or hopefully upgraded on Solana ecosystem as a whole? And what do you think it really means specifically for the institutions considering long term building things on SDP? Yeah, no, it's a great question. You know, it's so interesting. I feel like i've always felt a really strong connection to Solana ecosystem and the builders there. In part because when we looked when TRM was very early, we're looked around the space and were like, what are the important chains? Who are the important builders? And we really focused a lot of time and energy on ensuring that we had not only some coverage of Solana but really full coverage, really understanding the ecosystem, how the blockchain operates, and ensuring that it was safe. I would say in 2021, we were in an entirely different world when it came to Solana in particular. Certainly, the overall crypto ecosystem. But if you think about Solana, I think the promise has always been speed. But it was very very early from a liquidity standpoint we we certainly were not seeing um institutional but i think we knew we were going to see more and more activity that solana would really be sort of that the the it would be ethereum and solana would be sort of the way people would talk about this the permissionless blockchains and i think that's really how things have played out. But they played out it sort of an even more extraordinary way, right? We're seeing 600 billion in stable coin volume in February of 26 alone. We're seeing institutional, right? You know, build on Solana. So I think that if I think through where we were in 2021, I think we kind of understood what the promise of the blockchain was but i'm not sure i even appreciated that by 2026 we'd seen see sort of the level of institutional use adoption and quite frankly the liquidity that we see on solana today yeah i i definitely quote on that like 600 billion is a crazy number if you think about it i saw some of these kind of you know um in the launch a couple of weeks ago and then me kind of thinking through what we cover on Salon and really the growth of the service, and I was just blown away. Yeah, hopefully it will continue to grow and I think therefore, there's a lot more, even more demand on the compliance to get it right. So kind of tagging inside SDP a little bit here, as audience probably have seen the product demos that we have already released around Celana developer platform, we're trying to embed as much like compliance components inside the user experience as possible. Imagine you're product owner trying to create or issue stablecoin or tokenized deposits. You want to have all these different toolings to support you as you're a product owner to try and to create or issue stablecoins or tokenized deposits, you want to have all these different toolings to support you as you're making those decisions of, who are the KYC providers? Is this transaction legit, like pass all the sanctioning, rulings and stuff like that. I guess maybe even just with a sort of more future forward looking view as you thinking about the different features that's going to be really relevant to highlight within STP as we built these things out together with you guys. What do you think are the core kind of use experiences that you really want to showcase within STP? I think if you're, you know, you see the partners that are launching on STP, right, you're seeing the MasterCards and WorldPay in Western Union, right? These are some of the most like conservative, traditional financial institutions in the world that want to make sure that where their building, is safe and secure. And I think that's really sort of where we fit best into the ecosystem. Compliance isn't just sort of a tool set, it's actually like foundational infrastructure. And I think that SDP from like sort of day one really gets that. And that's what the partnership is really about. I think what we're building towards, when I think that SDP from day one really gets that and that's what the partnership is really about. What I think we're building towards what I think about, you know at launch and now beyond, is one where a regulated financial institution can make the decision to build on Solana, and immediately day one have the type of enterprise grade compliance capabilities that TRM offers. We are literally there to ensure that if you're building on Solana you know that you're not engaging with illicit actors that you have the necessary blockchain intelligence to sort of make those types of risk and compliance decisions. Yeah, absolutely i think it's also one of the really key things we're trying to hone into. A lot of the TradFi's sort of mindset, in a sense that it's not mutually exclusive that compliance and permissionless chains can't coexist, in fact. There's many great toolings, preventative measures and such that could allow any financial institution to transact in a very regulated way. I love that, I love that framing. When I think about this, I think about confidence. I think part of TRMs's role in the SDP, in the Solana ecosystem more broadly even, is that we want institutions that build on Solana to have confidence from day one that compliance is already solved, that they know that they're gonna be able to build safely and securely. I totally reject this idea that institutions shouldn't be building on permission-less blockchains, I think quite the opposite. I think the visibility, the traceability, the immutability of public blockchains make it the best place and potentially the safest place to build. Yeah, that's really well-put. Now, I guess just going back to about Solana as a whole, again, 2021 wasn't a great just going back to about solana as a whole, again, 2021 wasn't a great year necessarily to build on solana while I guess, you know, a lot of things happen in around 21, 22 period. But what stands out to you guys as you were like building directly on solana and continue to develop great tooling? Absolutely. I mean, look, it's always, have been been about speed and liquidity, but then I think there's also this really interesting ecosystem that has developed on Solana, which, to me, I had the real fortune of joining a hacker house in Brooklyn a couple of years ago, and I got to actually speak to a packed room of developers and technologists who are building on Solana today. And my takeaway from that experience, which honestly changed my view of the industry and what we're building in any respect, was like, wow, these people are some of the most creative people in the world who are building these incredibly cool things. But they all want, they all understand the importance of safety and security. Because the reality is none of this works if North Korea can steal billions of dollars importance of of safety and security because the reality is none of this works if you know north korea can steal billions of dollars you know at the speed of the internet if you see scams and fraud sort of proliferate and i think the reality is that like what solana's doing really leaning into sdp right now and just all of this work is to say hey we can build institutional on solana today and have safety and security as critical infrastructure on day one. Lili Brathwaite- Yeah. And I guess my last question is also just trying to dig in a little bit of the TRM offerings, because I think a lot of the times, and including back in the days when I was at Visa, looking at compliance, especially traditional compliance, tend to be retroactive, something happened, we don't know what it is. You then file a SAR report or something, and then you investigate. That's not great, because of course you want to have a much more preventative approach, proactive if you will, to be able to detect something before something happens. And I think that's especially important for an on-chain economy, especially somewhere on Solana in which really high throughput, very fast finality. We do things within milliseconds. So like, in those instances, of course you have a very rigorous and fast sort of infrastructure. Now, in order to then build that compliance tooling on top of it, and also trying to be as proactive as possible. Do you think that's possible? And also, how is CRM thinking about it? James Steadman, Jr.: I love that question. And we're thinking about it all the time. And I think there's a couple ways where we really have leaned in, particularly over the last year or so, we saw bad actors moving faster than ever before. Much of that is supercharged by artificial intelligence and allows for programmatic money laundering really at the speed of the internet and we've said all right we need to move as fast as the bad guys and we really sort of have implemented that in two ways one we created this really cool thing called the beacon network which is the largest public private partnership in crypto uh We have Coinbase, and Bainance, and Kraken, and OKEx, and HTx and Poloniex, about 85% of all centralized cryptocurrency transaction volume is part of the Beacon Network. We reached out to PayPal, and Robinhood and Stripe, and Thintex who've all joined. We've married them with about 70 law enforcement agencies, globally. Those law enforcement entities globally and those law enforcement entities are what we call flaggers where they'll flag illicit proceeds as they're moving in real time and send out an alert, think light house, beacon. And the exchange gets that alert and then they're able to block and work with law enforcement ultimately to seize those funds. And the reason I mentioned beacon in response to your question is, you know, we're seeing a world in which regular normal compliance practices don't work. Like they used to right when bad guys move at the speed of the internet and beacon was a way for us to solve this and I've loved to see how the community really has come together, uh, without regulation, right? Uh, to say hey, we want to stop bad actors from engaging in our platform. One of the coolest parts is it's not just centralized exchanges, we have DeFi protocols that are part of the beacon network that block funds that are flagged that are going to hit their platforms and send them off, you know, some work somewhere else. So there's there's all kinds of components that so that's one. And the two two is if bad actors are going to use ai to supercharge their operations we're using ai today across every layer of our platform uh in order to move faster so um you know the same tools that bad actors are using we're using to ensure that um this is not you know this is not compliance where we're checking a box or filing a SAR, this is compliance where you are responding and investigating in real time. That's really cool. I really want to have BEEQM within SDP as soon as possible. We are going to make that happen. I am. Yeah, Absolutely. I know our teams are working together and really, really excited about the prospects of that. That's awesome. Well, thank you so much, Ari, for being on the show. I really appreciate your time and also looking forward to the partnership. Such an honor Well thank you so much, Aary, for being on the show. Really appreciate your time and also looking forward to the partnership. Such an honor. Thank you so much, Katherine.
